Home Lko. ... on 8 May, 2025
Author: Vivek Chaudhary

Bench: Vivek Chaudhary
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench

Court No. - 10
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 1688 of 2025
Petitioner :- Monika Dwivedi And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
And Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Vaibhav Upadhyay
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Gaurav Shukla,Govind Narayan Shukla,Lalit Kishore Pandey,
Hon'ble Vivek Chaudhary,J.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petition seeks issuance of a writ in the nature of certiorari quashing First Information Report
dated 3.1.2025 bearing F.I.R./Case Crime No.2 of 2025, under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471, 506
I.P.C. at Police Station-Mahanagar, District-Lucknow.
3.  In this case, earlier Sections 467, 468 and 471 of I.P.C. were dropped against the petitioners by the Investigating Officer concerned during course of investigation.
Monika Dwivedi And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

sentences.text:

1 4.

Learned A.G.A., on instructions, states that the A.C.P. concerned on finding some shortcomings in the investigation, added Sections 467, 468 and 471 of I.P.C. again against the petitioners by order dated 31.1.2025 and a new Investigating Officer was also appointed in the case on 5.2.2025.
He further submits that petitioners also have criminal history, which they have not disclosed in the writ petition.

5. Further, as per report of the Mediation and Conciliation Centre of this Court dated 8.4.2025,
mediation has failed between the parties.
6. In view of above and also on the ground of concealment of criminal history, this Court is not inclined to exercise its discretionary jurisdiction.

7. From perusal of the impugned F.I.R. also, prima facie, a cognizable offence is made out against the petitioners, so the relief as claimed by the petitioners in the present petition cannot be granted under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
8.
Accordingly, writ petition is dismissed.

. 
[Brij Raj Singh,J.] [Vivek Chaudhary,J.]
Order Date :- 8.5.2025
